tier_reason: Peer-reviewed PPAM 2022 paper (Springer LNCS, DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-30442-2_22). Its Fig. 3 plots Cylon strong scaling against serial pandas v1.4, Dask and Modin on a 1B-row, two-int64-column dataset, with speed-up over pandas on a log axis. Not A: the scripts are public (cylondata/cylon_experiments), and GCC v9.4 and the Xeon Platinum 8160 CPU are stated, but the optimization flags are not.

corrections.caveats: Speed-ups appear only as dotted log-log lines in Fig. 3 (pandas_time/time), so there is no tabulated headline number. At parallelism 1 the paper says only that Cylon's C++ local operators 'perform on par or better than pandas'. The large multipliers come from running on up to 512 cores (15 nodes) against single-threaded serial pandas, so this is a distributed-vs-serial comparison. Past 256 the wall-clock time rises again at 512 because communication dominates. The paper says Dask and Modin are 'compared here only as a baseline'. Modin join failed at 1B rows, so a 100M-row run was used instead. Data is uniform random with cardinality C=0.9. Venue is the peer-reviewed PPAM 2022 conference (LNCS), not a Euro-Par workshop. The benchmark scripts are in cylondata/cylon_experiments, which has no license detected by GitHub. Optimization flags are unstated.

notes: Record is accurate apart from the venue caveat and last_commit. pushed_at is 2026-05-26, but the latest commit on the default branch is 2026-03-12, which is still active. Stars (302), Apache-2.0, not a fork and not archived were all verified via gh.

tier_reason: The Postgres comparison exists only as first-party README chart images: roughly 23x in 'Query Speed, X Faster than Postgres', plus three labelled ClickBench queries. Hardware is c6a.4xlarge with no CPU model, and no compiler or flags are given. The per-query gains are over 50x (about 283-1412x, derived) with flags unstated, which keeps it capped at C. ClickBench raw results corroborate the win against the 2022 PostgreSQL run but show parity against the 2025 run, so this was not upgraded to B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: The README chart 'Query Speed, X Faster than Postgres' puts Hydra at about 23x vanilla PostgreSQL. This is read off an unlabelled bar on a 0-25 axis; the same chart shows TimescaleDB ~10x, Citus Columnar ~4x and AWS Aurora ~2x. A second README chart (c6a.4xlarge, seconds) labels three ClickBench queries, Postgres vs Hydra: Count (Q0) 282.02s vs 0.55s, Sum (Q2) 263.07s vs 0.93s, Filtered count (Q1) 254.24s vs 0.18s. That is about 513x, 283x and 1412x (derived from page data). In the ClickBench raw results on c6a.4xlarge, Hydra 2022-12-09 vs PostgreSQL 2022-07-01 gives a geometric mean of ~23x, and Hydra 2023-09-19 gives ~25x, faster on all 43 queries (derived from ClickBench data). Against ClickBench's newer PostgreSQL 2025-02-26 result, the geometric mean is ~1.0x and Hydra 2023 is slower on 19 of 43 queries (derived from ClickBench data).
corrections.workload: ClickBench queries over the 100M-row hits dataset on AWS c6a.4xlarge, comparing Hydra columnar tables with vanilla PostgreSQL heap tables (README charts). The README says 42 queries; the ClickBench result files hold 43. The clickbench-100M and warehouse-10G suites in BENCHMARKS.md only track Hydra's own query times across releases and commits on Bencher.
corrections.license: AGPL-3.0 (the columnar engine in columnar/, per README and columnar/LICENSE) + Apache-2.0 (the rest of the repo; GitHub reports Apache-2.0 from the root LICENSE)
corrections.is_fork_of: citusdata/citus (Citus Columnar, src/backend/columnar), forked c. April 2022 per columnar/README.md
corrections.caveats: BENCHMARKS.md, the original benchmark_url, has no Postgres comparison: it only tracks Hydra's own timings through Bencher images. The Postgres win appears only in first-party README chart images, with no compiler or flags and no CPU model beyond c6a.4xlarge. Per-query README ratios exceed 50x. The ~23x aggregate matches ClickBench against its 2022 PostgreSQL run, but ClickBench's 2025-02-26 PostgreSQL result is roughly at parity with Hydra 2023 (geometric mean ~1.0, Hydra slower on 19 of 43 queries; derived). The current ClickBench 'hydra' entry (2025-03-04) is Hydra's serverless OLAP service, not this extension. The columnar engine is AGPL-3.0 (copyleft), and the code is a fork of Citus Columnar. The last commit was 2025-02-10, so the repo is stale.

notes: The record's benchmark_url, BENCHMARKS.md, only charts Hydra's own timings; the Postgres comparison lives in the README charts, so the URL was repointed. hydradatabase/hydra now redirects to hydradatabase/columnar. Stars (3043), last commit 2025-02-10 (stale), not archived and not a GitHub fork were all verified. The license was misreported as plain Apache-2.0; the engine itself is AGPL-3.0, which is still OSI-approved, so usability stays copyable.
